## 12. Implementation notes for the JS port

1. Model the block-HTML extractor as a tag-balance scanner over a proper HTML tokenizer, not a blank-line-delimited CommonMark HTML block.
2. Recognition requires a block-level tag at column 0 (case-insensitive name lookup against the §1 list). Otherwise the line is markdown and any HTML on it is inline-raw.
3. Once a block is extracted from a line, continue scanning the same line's remainder for further block-level HTML (producing extra split lines and, for void elements/comments, relocation after the following paragraph). If the line did not start with a block tag, do not extract at all.
4. Unbalanced open tag → consume verbatim to EOF (including blank lines). Incomplete closing tag (``) → emit what was consumed and **drop the rest**. Unclosed comment → not a block, escape `<`. Unclosed PI → append `\n\n?>`.
5. Separator rule: join top-level items with `\n`, but emit `\n\n` after a raw block-HTML item that was followed by a blank line and by further content; strip leading/trailing blank lines; collapse runs of blank lines to one.
6. `--a` pipeline must include md_in_html (`markdown="1"|"block"|"span"`): strip the `markdown` attribute, process the interior as markdown/inline, and re-serialize the wrapper element with normalized attributes (`name="value"` double-quoted, booleans as `name="name"`, source order preserved) and children at column 0. `--b`, `--c`, and the combined pass must NOT.
7. Getting §11 exactly right requires the combined pass to be the same code path as passes 1–3 with the extension set empty — do not shortcut it to string concatenation, because of divergence classes (a) and (b).
